items.title: The Picard group of the generic fibre vanishes for a flat essentially finite type local algebra over a valuation ring with regular special fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a valuation ring R with fraction field K and residue field kappa, and a ring homomorphism R -> A such that A is local and R -> A is local, A is flat and essentially of finite type over R, and A tensor_R kappa is regular; it concludes that Pic(A tensor_R K) = 0 (source lines 36845-36856). The proof is a long descent. Starting with an invertible A tensor_R K-module L, it uses that L is finite and the construct-finite-module lemma to find a finite A-module M with M tensor_R K isomorphic to L, which may be taken torsion free as an R-module and hence flat over R by the valuation-ring criterion (proof lines 36859-36865). From the flat finite type statement over a valuation ring the proof deduces that M is finitely presented as an A-module and that A is essentially of finite presentation as an R-algebra (proof lines 36866-36868). The structure of relatively perfect modules then shows M is perfect relative to R, in particular pseudo-coherent as an A-module, and the perfect-over-a-regular-local-ring statement upgrades this to M being perfect, so that M has a finite free resolution F_bullet over A (proof lines 36869-36874). It follows that L is quasi-isomorphic to a finite complex of free A tensor_R K-modules, so the Euler characteristic map gives [L] = n[A tensor_R K] in K_0(A tensor_R K) for some integer n (proof lines 36875-36879). Applying the determinant map then shows L is trivial, which is the conclusion (proof lines 36880-36881). The non-routine content is the chain of upgrades from a finite torsion free module to a perfect module with a finite free resolution, and the final use of the determinant on K_0.
